findings.title: `except OSError` in `resume_item` mislabels unrelated failures as report-write failures
findings.description: `resume_item` ends with `except OSError` and returns `HALTED` with "cannot write the batch report". Its comment assumes only a report write can raise `OSError`. `_validate` calls `load_pipeline(state.pipeline)`, and `loader.load_pipeline` documents that it raises `FileNotFoundError` (an `OSError` subclass) when the pipeline is gone. A pipeline file deleted or renamed since the run started therefore returns exit 3 (HALTED) with a message about the report, which is wrong. It should be REJECTED (exit 2) with an accurate message. This branch also logs nothing itself. It relies on `_write_atomic` having logged, which is false for every other `OSError` source. Catch `FileNotFoundError` around `load_pipeline` in `_validate` and turn it into a `_Stop(REJECTED, ...)`. Narrow the `OSError` handler to the report writes, or have it log with `_logger.exception`. A test should cover the missing-pipeline case.

findings.title: `_write_atomic` leaks temp files when the write or rename fails
findings.description: The temp file is created with `delete=False`. If `handle.write` or `temp.replace(target)` raises `OSError`, the handler logs and re-raises but never unlinks the temp file. Each failed write, such as a full disk, leaves a `.{name}.<random>` file in the runs dir, and the report is rewritten after every item. `test_a_failed_write_keeps_the_previous_report_and_logs_error` patches `Path.replace` to fail and so exercises this path, but it asserts nothing about leftover files. Unlink the temp file in the failure path (a `try/finally` with `missing_ok=True`) and assert that the runs dir holds no stray files after the failed write.

findings.title: The mutating-step allowlist in `pipeline_mutates` is fail-open
findings.description: `_MUTATING_STEP_TYPES` hard-codes five `StepTypeName` members. Any step type added later (`StepTypeName` currently also has `dispatch`, `compact`, `gate` and `fan_out`) is treated as non-mutating and runs without the project lock. That fails silently and breaks the open/closed principle: each new step type needs an edit in a separate module, with nothing to remind the author. Make "mutates the checkout" a declared property of the step type (as the registry already does for other behaviour). Alternatively, add a test that enumerates `StepTypeName` and requires each member to be classified explicitly.

findings.title: `_locked` builds a coroutine before the lock is taken, then closes it on failure
findings.description: `_locked` receives an already-created coroutine and must call `run_coroutine.close()` if the lock is refused. `ExitStack` and `_take_run_lock(stack, ...)` wrap what is really one optional context manager. This contradicts the project rule to resist complexity. Pass a zero-argument factory, or use `with project_run_lock(os.getcwd()) if pipeline_mutates(definition) else nullcontext():`. Then no coroutine can be left unawaited and the `ExitStack` goes away. Five call sites would simplify.

findings.title: `run_item` imports private functions from `run.py` through a lazy circular import
findings.description: `handle_item_resume` imports `_apply_param_overrides` and `_run_pipeline_sdk` from `run.py` inside the function (pyright private-usage suppressions included). `run.py` in turn imports `run_item`. This is a cycle worked around at runtime, and it reaches into another module's private API. Move the shared runner and param-override helpers into a module that both import. Alternatively, have `run.py` pass them in, since `resume_item` already takes `run_body` by injection.

findings.title: Blocking subprocess work runs inside `async def` functions
findings.description: `_resume_locked`, `_select_item`, `_open_dependencies` and `_git_precondition` run on the event loop. `_git_precondition` is called synchronously from `_resume_locked`. They synchronously call `project_run_lock` (via `git rev-parse`), `dirty_paths`, `restore_target`, `run_git(["merge-base", ...])`, `verify_git_state`, and the `cf_client.list_slices` / `list_tasks` subprocess wrappers. The Python rules require sync work inside async functions to complete in under 1 ms or go through an executor. Practical impact is low, because `asyncio.run` hosts a single task at the CLI boundary. The rule is still unmet, and the executor path already uses `asyncio.to_thread` for the report write. Either wrap the git and cf phase in `asyncio.to_thread`, or make that phase a plain function and keep only `run_body` and `evaluate_each_source` async.

findings.title: `cf_client: Any` erases the contract at several new boundaries
findings.description: `resume_item`, `_select_item`, `_git_precondition` and `_open_dependencies` all take `cf_client: Any`, and `item_resume.py` calls `cf_client.list_slices(...)` on it. `branch_ops` already defines a `CfClientProtocol`. Using a Protocol, as the project's "program to interfaces" rule says, would let strict pyright check the calls. `BodyRunner` also returns `Awaitable[object]`. That makes `run_body`'s result unused by design, but it hides that the real contract is `rerun.record` being set as a side effect. Nothing at the type level connects a successful body run to `rerun.record`. The `rerun.record is None` check is the only guard.

findings.title: Test helpers and tests break the strict-typing rule
findings.description: The Python rules require strict pyright over `tests/` and type hints on all function signatures. New helpers carry `# type: ignore[no-untyped-def]` (`body_runner`, `resume`, `_record`) and return `object`. Tests silence attribute access with `# type: ignore[attr-defined]`, for example `_fresh_p6()` in `test_run_lock_cli.py` and the `outcome.exit` accesses in `test_item_resume_validation.py`. Type the helpers (`BodyRunner`, `ResumeOutcome`, `Result` from `typer.testing`). `test_run_lock_cli.py` also replaces the whole `asyncio` and `sys` modules inside `run.py` with mocks. That is the monkeypatching-internals symptom the DIP rule warns about, and it would hide any other use of those modules in `run.py`.

findings.title: `item_params` mutates inside a generator expression
findings.description: `sorted(key for key in RESERVED_PARAMS if params.pop(key, None) is not None)` removes keys as a side effect of building the "dropped" list. A reserved key stored with a `None` value is removed without being reported, and the comprehension hides the mutation. Make it explicit: `dropped = [k for k in RESERVED_PARAMS if k in params]`, then pop each one. Also, `run.py:1201` uses `assert decision is not None` as a runtime guard, which `-O` strips. A real guard or a narrowed return type from `check_item_flags` would be safer.

findings.title: Duplicate "replace the record by index" logic
findings.description: `_reconcile` and `ItemRerun.replace` (batch_report.py) both locate a record with `next(i for i, r in enumerate(records) if r.index == ...)` and overwrite it. A shared `BatchReport.replace_record(record)` would remove the duplicate. It would also give the "record not found" case an explicit error instead of a bare `StopIteration`.

findings.title: An interrupted batch leaves unreached items without records
findings.description: Only a `GitEnvironmentError` halt appends `not_run` records for unreached items. Other exceptions end the run through the `in_flight` path, for example a lost session or `KeyboardInterrupt`. These record only the in-flight item. Items after it have no report entry, so `--item N` on one is refused with "no record for item N". That matches the stated D7 scope, but a Ctrl-C mid-batch is a common way to end one. It is worth confirming as intended and documenting.

findings.title: Lock acquisition, reserved-param enforcement and report persistence are well covered
findings.description: `project_run_lock` takes a non-blocking `flock`, closes the descriptor on every failure path, and logs each refusal at ERROR. `control_params.py` defines the reserved keys once, and they are enforced in the CLI, the loader and `item_params`. Report JSON round-trip, version-mismatch and corrupt-file handling raise a typed `BatchReportLoadError` with the path named. Tests cover the held lock, a killed holder, separate worktrees, git-dir failure and an unopenable lock file. The line length (104) and the ruff rule set in `pyproject.toml` match what the new code uses.
